adjudications.evidence_summary: create_order commits the inserted order before attempting the audit write. With fail_audit=True, it then raises before inserting the audit record; the targeted case test reproduces the resulting partial state with order_count equal to 1 instead of the required 0.
adjudications.scope_assessment: The failure occurs in the supplied create_order implementation through its explicit fail_audit path and violates the atomicity invariant stated by the case test, so it applies directly to supported case behavior rather than a hypothetical caller or infrastructure condition.
adjudications.materiality_assessment: Persisting an order without its required audit record creates inconsistent durable business state and compromises data integrity, making the defect materially production-relevant.

findings.claim: create_order can durably persist an order without its required audit record when the audit step fails, leaving partial business state.
evidence: evals/cases/case_01/src/orders.py:17-25 inserts the order and commits it before attempting the audit write at lines 30-34.
evals/cases/case_01/src/orders.py:27-28 raises RuntimeError after the order commit when fail_audit=True, so the function exits before creating an audit record.

Running pytest -q evals/cases/case_01 produced 1 failed and 1 passed test; test_failed_business_operation_leaves_no_partial_state observed order_count == 1 after the simulated audit failure, contradicting the required atomic outcome of zero persisted orders and zero audit records.
